policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Presence or absence of the article before Ἰησοῦς is invisible in English; ASV 'When Jesus had spoken these words' renders either. No mapped textual note; both marginal notes are alternative_rendering.

ASV's text reads the singular indeclinable proper name, 'the brook Kidron' (τοῦ Κεδρών), and relegates the plural common noun 'of the Cedars' (τῶν Κέδρων) to the margin; the rendered text distinguishes the singular article.
Article before Ἰησοῦς; ASV 'for Jesus oft-times resorted thither' renders either reading identically.
ASV 'officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees' uses one 'from' and the definite article English idiom requires; it neither shows nor excludes a repeated ἐκ τῶν before Φαρισαίων.
ASV renders an inferential connective, 'Jesus therefore, knowing all the things', which answers οὖν; δὲ would give 'and/but'.

ASV 'went forth, and saith unto them' has a finite aorist plus a present verb, matching ἐξῆλθεν καὶ λέγει and excluding RP's participle-plus-aorist ἐξελθὼν εἶπεν. r00-base and r01 are the same reading differing only in punctuation spacing, which English cannot distinguish.
ASV names the subject in its text, 'Jesus saith unto them, I am he', where the base reading has only λέγει αὐτοῖς with the subject carried over; the explicit name answers ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
The added ὅτι is recitative, introducing direct speech; ASV 'when therefore he said unto them, I am he' renders it with the comma alone, so English cannot distinguish.
Word order only (ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς / αὐτούς ἐπηρώτησεν); ASV 'he asked them' fixes English order regardless.
ὠτάριον and ὠτίον are alternative diminutives of the same noun; ASV 'his right ear' renders either.
ASV reads 'Put up the sword into the sheath' with no possessive; the added σου would give 'thy sword', which ASV renders elsewhere when present.
ASV 'and led him to Annas first' supplies the object pronoun English requires either way, and 'led' does not decide between ἤγαγον and the compound ἀπήγαγον.
ASV 'that one man should die for the people' renders ἀποθανεῖν; ἀπολέσθαι would give 'perish'.
Article before ἄλλος μαθητής; ASV 'and so did another disciple' cannot show its presence or absence.
ASV 'the other disciple, who was known unto the high priest' renders an attributive articular phrase and a ὅς ἦν relative clause alike; English idiom supplies the relative either way.
Genitive τοῦ ἀρχιερέως versus dative τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ after γνωστός; ASV renders both as 'known unto the high priest', as its identical wording in v.15 shows.
Word order of the indirect object and subject only; ASV 'The maid therefore that kept the door saith unto Peter' follows English order regardless.
ASV 'and Peter also was with them' renders the adjunctive καί with 'also'; the RP reading lacks καί and would give simply 'and Peter was with them'.
Article before Ἰησοῦς; ASV 'Jesus answered him' renders either.
ASV 'I have spoken openly to the world' is a perfect, answering λελάληκα; the aorist ἐλάλησα would give 'I spake', as ASV in fact writes later in the same verse for ἐλάλησα.
ASV 'where all the Jews come together' renders the adjective πάντες; πάντοτε would give 'always'.
ASV 'Why askest thou me? ask them that have heard me' does not distinguish simplex ἐρωτάω from compound ἐπερωτάω, both rendered 'ask'; r00-base and r01 differ only in punctuation spacing.
Word order of participle and genitive only; ASV 'one of the officers standing by' is fixed by English order.
Article before Ἰησοῦς; ASV 'Jesus answered him' renders either.
ASV 'Annas therefore sent him bound' renders the connective οὖν, which the RP reading omits.

ASV 'He denied, and said, I am not' has no connective at the denial, while it renders the οὖν of the preceding clause as 'They said therefore unto him'; the added οὖν is thus absent from the ASV's text.
Article before Πέτρος; ASV 'Peter therefore denied again' renders either.
ASV 'that they might not be defiled, but might eat the passover' carries the purpose sense across the conjunction by ellipsis; a second ἵνα need not surface separately in English.
ἐξῆλθεν already means 'went out', so ASV 'Pilate therefore went out unto them' renders the reading with or without the pleonastic ἔξω.
ASV 'and saith' is a present, answering φησίν; the aorist εἶπεν would give 'and said'.
ASV 'bring ye against this man' renders κατά with the genitive and equally the bare genitive of the charge; 'against' is required by the noun 'accusation' either way.
ASV 'an evil-doer' serves both the participial phrase κακὸν ποιῶν and the noun κακοποιός; the English noun does not exclude the participle.
Presence of the article is invisible in English here; ASV's wording renders either.
ASV 'The Jews said unto him' has no connective, while it renders the earlier οὖν of the same verse as 'Pilate therefore said'; the added οὖν is absent from the ASV's text.
Position of πάλιν only; ASV 'entered again into the Praetorium' fixes English order regardless.
ASV 'Jesus answered' has no indirect object; the added αὐτῷ would give 'Jesus answered him', as ASV writes at vv. 20 and 23 where αὐτῷ stands.
ASV 'of thyself' renders ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ and equally the Koine ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτοῦ used for the second person; the English reflexive does not distinguish them.
Word order of verb and pronoun only; ASV 'did others tell it thee' follows English order regardless.
Position of ἄν within the apodosis only; ASV 'then would my servants fight' is unaffected.
Presence of the article is invisible in English; ASV's wording renders either. The verse's only note is alternative_rendering and concerns English wording.
ASV 'that I am a king' must supply the subject pronoun in English whether or not emphatic ἐγώ stands in the Greek.
Word order only; ASV 'I find no crime in him' follows English order regardless.
Word order of ἀπολύσω and ὑμῖν only; ASV 'that I should release unto you one' fixes English order regardless.
Word order of ἀπολύσω and ὑμῖν only; ASV 'that I release unto you the King of the Jews' fixes English order regardless.
ASV 'They cried out therefore again, saying' renders πάλιν alone; the added πάντες would give 'all' before the verb.
